title: Pin the study instance's repo ref in core and test dispatch calls it
summary: When a study job starts, athena-core resolves the repo URL and ref from the study instance's config to a SHA through a Pinner trait. It records the SHA in the Job record and mounts the pinned tree read-only in the agents' working directory. Nothing is hard-coded to firstmate, and a dispatch-level test with a fake pinner proves run.rs calls it.

defaults_applied.how: Dispatch-level and real-pinner tests, with clippy and fmt clean.
Behavior criteria are runnable with cargo test.
Docs and the decision record are written for outside readers.
Tests use local file:// repos and no secrets are added.
A test fails if the run.rs pin call is removed.

assumptions: pin.rs is absent at this commit because the earlier attempt was rejected, so it is recreated.
The study instance config table carries the repo URL and ref; if it lacks them, no pin is made, or the job fails clearly.
The real pinner shells out to git (ls-remote and a shallow fetch or checkout) rather than adding a git crate.
Read-only is enforced by file permissions plus agent policy; a hard OS-level mount is not required.

acceptance_criteria.text: athena-core has a Pinner trait with a real git-based implementation that resolves a repo URL and ref to a full 40-hex SHA and checks out that tree. The core, not an agent, makes the call.
The repo URL and ref come from the study instance's config (for example athena.toml). No firstmate URL or 'main' is hard-coded in Rust source; firstmate appears only as config or docs examples.
run.rs calls the pinner only for the study capability, before the prediction commit. It stores URL, ref and SHA in a new optional Job record field. The change capability never calls the pinner.
The pinned tree is mounted read-only in the working directory of both producer and verifier. Docs say how read-only is enforced.

A dispatch-level test builds Athena with a counting fake pinner and a scripted fake agent driver on the study capability. It asserts exactly one pinner call, the fake SHA in the Job record, and the mount existing in the agent working directory. Run `cargo test -p athena-core`.
A dispatch-level test with the real Change capability and the same counting fake pinner asserts zero calls and no pin in the Job record. Run `cargo test`.

Real-pinner unit tests use a local file:// repo in a temp dir, with no network. They cover resolving the ref to the expected SHA, an error on a missing ref, and the read-only mount. Run `cargo test -p athena-core`.
`cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` pass. Removing the pin call in run.rs would fail at least one test.
The decision record (alternatives, reversal cost) is in docs/decisions.md and CHANGELOG.md notes the change. The diff has no secrets and no network-dependent tests.

out_of_scope: Changing study prompts beyond pointing at the mount path
departures: Cost and time are raised above the reference because the change touches core dispatch, adds a trait, and needs scripted fake-driver tests.
